concepts.title: Tangents to a Circle
concepts.definition: A tangent to a circle is a line that meets the circle at exactly one point, the point of contact; from an external point exactly two tangents can be drawn, while a point on the circle gives one and a point inside gives none.
concepts.key_idea: Touch, not cut: a tangent meets the circle once, and external points own two of them.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh110.txt sections 10.1-10.2 (introduction, tangent to a circle)
question_patterns: define a tangent to a circle - how is it different from a secant
how many tangents can be drawn from a point inside the circle
how many tangents can be drawn from an external point
what is the point of contact of a tangent
draw tangents to the circle from the given external point
classify the given line positions as secant, tangent or non-intersecting

solution_steps.explain: Count where the line meets the circle - one point means tangent.
Outside gives two tangents, on the circle one, inside none.
The single common point is the point of contact.

concepts.title: Tangent Perpendicular to Radius
concepts.definition: The tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact - the theorem that anchors every tangent computation and construction.
concepts.key_idea: Touch point rule: radius meets tangent at right angles.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh110.txt theorem on tangent and radius
question_patterns: prove that the tangent at any point of a circle is perpendicular to the radius
the radius is given - draw the tangent at the point and justify
why must the shortest distance from the centre be along the radius
find the angle between the tangent and the radius at the point of contact
apply the perpendicularity theorem to the given figure
state the theorem about tangent and radius with a diagram

solution_steps.explain: Draw the radius through the point of contact.
Any other line through the point must cut the circle twice.
Only the perpendicular line touches once - it is the tangent.

concepts.title: Length of a Tangent from an External Point
concepts.definition: The two tangents drawn from an external point to a circle have equal lengths; with centre O, external point P and contact point T, the right triangle OPT gives the tangent length as the square root of (d squared minus r squared), where d is OP.
concepts.key_idea: Two equal tangents from one point; the right triangle OPT computes their length.
concepts.textbook_ref: jemh110.txt theorem on lengths of tangents and its applications
question_patterns: prove that the lengths of tangents from an external point are equal
find the length of the tangent from a point at the given distance from the centre
the tangents from P touch the circle at Q and R - prove PQ = PR
find the radius when the tangent length and distance are given
use the right triangle formed by centre, external point and contact point
solve the given tangent quadrilateral problem

solution_steps.explain: Distance squared minus radius squared gives tangent squared.
The root is the tangent length.

worked_examples.question_pattern: From a point {d} cm from the centre of a circle of radius {r} cm, find the length of the tangent.

extracted_variables.d: distance of the external point from the centre in cm
extracted_variables.r: radius of the circle in cm

solution_template.explain: d squared minus r squared gives tangent squared.
The root is the tangent length.
